How Mania works
Mania RatingHow strong his role and production have been this season, compared with other players at his position. It blends production, volume, team role, red-zone work and efficiency.
Week RatingHis Mania Rating adjusted for this week: the opponent, how players with a similar role have done against that defense, and his recent usage.
Percentiles and colorsEvery bar shows where he ranks among players at his position. Green is the top 30%, yellow is the middle, red is the bottom 40%.

Calling Fantasy Mania one of the best rating systems in the world is our own opinion, not an official ranking or an independent audit. Accuracy numbers come from our own tests on past seasons.

How to read this

Week report

Injuries

Who is hurt, whether he is a starter, and who picks up the work. The points are the change to the replacement's Week rating, and they lean on how that player actually did in games the injured player missed.

Through Week

Buy Low / Sell High

Players whose role and fantasy points disagree. Usage is how much work he gets: volume, team role and red-zone chances. Production is the points and yards he has turned it into. Both are percentiles at his position.

This compares usage and production so far this season. It flags a player who left his last game early or missed it, but it does not see injury reports, depth-chart changes or a new quarterback, and this early a game or two can swing it. Treat it as a list of names to look into, not a trade verdict.

Through Week

Defense vs. Position

What each defense has given up to running backs, receivers and tight ends. "Vs usual" compares what players scored against this defense with what those same players normally score, so a defense is not punished for a schedule full of great offenses.

Easiest matchups first. Green defenses have allowed 10%+ more than usual, red ones 10%+ less.
Week onward

Schedule Strength

Every team's remaining opponents, graded by what those defenses have given up to the position so far. It is the "vs usual" number from Defense vs. Position, looked up for each game still to come. Easiest schedules first.

Green is a defense allowing 10%+ more than usual to the position, red is 10%+ less. This early most defenses have only a few games behind them, so expect these to move.
Week results

Report Card

How the Week ratings held up. These are the ratings the model gives using only the games before Week , set against what each player then scored.

Compare Players

Overall value and Week start decision. Change the games used for either player and the model recalculates.
